records.claim: From 1 June 2026, a Swedish work permit generally requires employment conditions meeting the applicable rules, including a salary of at least 90 percent of Sweden's median salary under the new work-permit salary requirement.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency salary-requirement guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed 90% of median salary for covered first-time work-permit decisions from 1 June 2026; current threshold is SEK 34,470/month for applications received from 16 June 2026. Transitional and exempt categories remain applicable.

records.claim: Applicants for a Swedish higher-education study residence permit in 2026 must normally demonstrate at least SEK 10,656 per month for maintenance, with possible reductions where free food or housing is provided.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency higher-education permit guidance on 2026-10-11. Confirmed SEK 10,656/month for 2026 applications, possible reductions for free food/housing, additional family maintenance, and the current 15-hour weekly work limit for bachelor's/master's permits granted on or after 11 June 2026.

records.claim: Eligible graduates who completed a qualifying higher-education programme lasting at least two semesters may apply before their current permit expires for a residence permit of up to one year (bachelor's/master's) or up to 18 months (doctoral studies) to seek work or explore starting a business, subject to financial maintenance and insurance conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swedish Migration Agency post-study guidance on 2026-10-11, including programme-completion, application timing, financial maintenance, insurance and permit-duration conditions.
